Roston Chase to Ruturaj Gaikwad, 1 run, and a nudge to mid-on off the front foot is all it takes to close out this record-breaking game. Only the second time a 400+ target has been hunted down, after that legendary 438 by South Africa in 2006.

22:12 Local Time, 16:42 GMT, 22:12 IST: Brilliance, cruelty, mediocrity - what a ride it was today. The team batting second hardly broke their belief even when the target was 406. And a player who is not just their captain, but the No. 1 ODI batter now, led the show. Campbell, Jangoo, Hope ran the show in the first innings. Gill and Rohit took the baton from them and put on an epic 255-run opening stand. The bowling was ordinary on a lot of occasions, but the batting was unbelievably fearless overall. Batters forced the bowlers to give up. It didn't feel like an ODI for most parts. It resembled a T20 game where batters came and swung freely without fear. And the alarming part was they were able to be that bossy for 80 odd overs. To think that India chased down 406 with 39 balls to spare - to be honest it could have been over even earlier had they pressed harder at the end - with 8 wickets in hand is simply outrageous.

Rohit Sharma (1/2): [On his 35th ODI hundred and the meaning behind his celebration] I keep that celebration for myself. Ah, it's for me. It's for me. Some things are just meant to be with you. It's not to be shared. So yeah, that was for me. [On batting with Gill and their 200-plus run partnership while chasing 400] Yeah, absolutely. I think, like you said, wicket was good. We just wanted to continue to keep batting. We were not thinking too much about the scoreboard, to be honest. We were just trying to play according to the merit of the ball, and we kept stitching the partnership, which was, I think, when you're chasing a target like that, you need to keep stitching big partnership, and that's what we did. Gill was fantastic on the other side, very much in control of his batting the entire innings, and to stay not out till the end was fantastic to see as well.

A day to remember for the ball-bashers, a day to forget for the bowlers. With these small boundaries and such flat pitches, no score is safe. Imagine, India chased down 406 with 6.3 overs to spare without dew. Had there been dew, where will the bowlers hide? But to dominate the bowlers this way needs skill. And Shubman was top drawer. Rohit was enjoyable. Jangoo and Campell were outstanding and Shai Hope was smart. Two games straight where the bowlers struggled in the powerplay. West Indies have leaked 706 runs in 85.1 overs and picked just 4 wickets across two games. And to think that next game is in Gill's own backyard, where it could be another road rolled out, good luck being a bowler! That's it for tonight. We will be back on Saturday nice and early.
